purpose: Replace invalid nested-family classification for the F1b R2 action-policy problem with prospective recovery of explicit structural restrictions inside an encompassing flexible action surface.

encompassing_surface.equation: u = b + beta_b*(2B-1) + beta_a*A + beta_r*R + beta_ab*A*(2B-1) + beta_ar*A*R

additive.interpretation: No accuracy-by-belief or accuracy-by-reward interaction in the encompassing surface.

cbd_complement.interpretation: Exact observable-surface restriction implied by the current CBD complement action equation for binary accuracy cue.

nesting_statement.reason: The flexible AP-GENERAL surface can exactly reproduce AP-B and the current CBD AP-A surface, so held-out prediction need not uniquely identify one nested label.

departure_design.requirement: Weak/moderate/strong departures must be generated at prospectively controlled utility-space distance from the CBD restricted manifold, not only by arbitrary coefficient perturbation.

recovery_metrics: false-rejection probability under each restriction null
detection probability by departure distance and violation axis
interpretation_boundary: Failure to reject a restriction is not proof that the restriction is the true human mechanism.
Both ADD and CBD restrictions may be simultaneously not rejected when the generated or observed surface lies near their intersection.
Rejecting both restrictions supports only departure from those declared structures, not a unique alternative psychological mechanism.
The candidate distance grid is for design search and is not an empirical effect-size calibration.
No result from this contract authorizes human recruitment, F1b runtime activation, or an M0 equation change.

method_basis.role: Nested candidate models can be difficult to identify; parameter ranges can make restricted and flexible models effectively indistinguishable.
Simulation-calibrated likelihood-ratio testing is used for nested mixed models when standard reference distributions are unreliable.
